sections.history: Tiruppalliyin Mukkudal, also recorded as Kekkarai, lies about 6–7 km north-east of Tiruvarur in Tiruvarur district, in the Kaveri delta. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). The name mukkudal, 'the meeting of three,' marks it as a place at a confluence of waters. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Mukkonanatheswarar — also Tirunethranathar and Trinethranathar, names of the three-eyed Shiva — in the sanctum, with the goddess Anjanakshi, also called Mayilmevum Kanni, in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The temple keeps the simple, well-ordered plan of the smaller Kaveri-country sanctuaries.
sections.legends: The lord's names dwell on the eye of Shiva: Tirunethranathar and Trinethranathar name the three-eyed one, whose third eye is the eye of wisdom and of the burning away of ignorance. The goddess Anjanakshi is 'she of the collyrium-dark eyes,' and in the Tamil Mayilmevum Kanni, 'the maiden with the peacock,' she carries a gentler grace. As with many smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana is kept chiefly in local tradition and the Tevaram verses of Appar.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine near Tiruvarur. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail around Tiruvarur include Mukkudal among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruppalliyin Mukkudal the pilgrim comes to a quiet shrine of the three-eyed lord at a meeting of waters. Before Mukkonanatheswarar and Anjanakshi, the visitor finds a small Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur country, its names turning the mind to the eye of Shiva and the peace of the confluence.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruppalliyin Mukkudal (Kekkarai) is about 6–7 km north-east of Tiruvarur in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with local buses and taxis to the village.
